To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MDSC in fresh blood samples are more resistant to the freezing and thawing procedure than the MDSC in cryopreserved samples.

the frequency of MDSC subsets and their function in terms of suppressor activity and Arginase I or ROS production are altered after cryopreservation, and that these changes are dependent on the MDSC subset.
the frequency of myeloid-derived suppressive cell (MDSC) subsets and their functions are significantly reduced after cryogenic storage of human peripheral blood mononucleated cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of myeloid-derived suppressive cells in fresh and cryogenically stored blood samples from healthy donors and patients with different cancers.
the study of MDSC, a heterogeneous population of immature cells that are found in the peripheral blood of cancer patients and healthy subjects.
the development of guidelines for the reliable assessment of the frequency and functions of MDSC in human peripheral blood samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most reliable assessment of MDSC frequency, function, and phenotype in human blood is performed in fresh samples.
the frequency of the MDSC subsets in the blood of healthy donors or cancer patients is significantly decreased after cryopreservation and that this decrease is not uniform for all MDSC subsets.
MDSC are best analyzed fresh, if at all possible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MDSC are heterogeneous and that they can be identified and characterized by a variety of markers.
the cryopreservation of blood samples for the assessment of MDSC subsets and their function should be avoided.
cryopreserved PBMC are not suitable for the analysis of MDSC subsets, especially DR⁻/CD14+ and GR⁻/CD34+ MDSC, which are the most abundant MDSC in human PBMC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the frequency of MDSC is significantly affected by the cryopreservation and thawing procedures, which should be taken into consideration when analyzing MDSC in fresh and cryo-preserved samples.
the frequency of MDSC is significantly reduced after cryostorage, especially in the DR⁻ / LIN⁻ / CD15+ and DR ⁻ / LIN⁍ / CD33+ subsets.

the MDSC frequency and function can be assessed in cryopreserved samples, but it is necessary to monitor the frequency of the DR⁻ /CD11b⁺ and DR⁻ / CD14⁺ cells, which are more resistant to cryopreservation than the DR⁻CD15⁺ and DR(-/lo)/CD33+ cells.
